D.treatment: activities pitched at the edge of current learning
D.comparison: activities at the same level as current ability

cells.quote: It is both common sense and demonstrated in the literature that students learn more quickly and deeply when they engage in classroom activities pitched at the edge of their current learning.
cells.note: Definitional/argumentative claim in the brief; no new study data or printed effect size.

D.treatment: activities pitched at the edge of current learning
D.comparison: learning expectations far beyond current capacity

cells.quote:
It is both common sense and demonstrated in the literature that students learn more quickly and deeply when they engage in classroom activities pitched at the edge of their current learning.

Learning is not as effective when it is at the same level as what students already know and can do independently (too easy) or when learning expectations are far beyond their current capacity (too frustrating).
cells.note: The brief presents this as a literature-supported argument about Vygotsky's zone of proximal development, not as a new empirical comparison.

D.treatment: access to scaffolded, challenging content and coursework
D.comparison: students' level of English proficiency as a predictor

cells.quote: Research has found that giving English learners access to scaffolded, challenging content and coursework is a better predictor of achievement than “students’ level of English proficiency.”
cells.note: This is a narrative report of cited research comparing predictors, rather than a new treatment experiment; the text does not provide a pooled effect size or study design.
